chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from one of his companions who said:

The Marzaban asked Al-Reza (peace be upon him) about the slaughter of the child before he attains puberty, and the slaughter of the woman. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem with the slaughter of the eunuch, and the child, and the woman, when there is desperation to it'.
ai.seo_question: Is the slaughter of a child, eunuch, or woman valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi*, this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the slaughter performed by children, eunuchs, and women is valid (*la ba'sa*) specifically under conditions of necessity (*idhtarru*), reflecting the Shia principle of *darura* (necessity) overriding standard requirements. This ruling distinguishes between the general validity of their slaughter and the stricter conditions often applied to non-male adult males, ensuring food security during times of scarcity or when no other qualified slaughterer is available.
